PyTorch defines L2 normalization as `x / max(||x||₂, eps)`; default `eps=1e-12` prevents division by zero but does not ensure moderate gradients. Mathematical implication: below the floor, the Jacobian is `I/eps`; above it, its scale is proportional to `1/||x||₂`. Tiny embeddings can therefore amplify gradients substantially. Detaching the denominator removes its derivative but retains reciprocal-scale amplification; it changes backward behavior without fixing small-norm instability. [Normalization documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.functional.normalize.html), [detach documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.Tensor.detach.html).

PyTorch recommends disabling autocast locally and explicitly casting inputs to float32 for sensitive calculations. For the HSTU scale-matched residual, compute norms, clamping, scale ratios and residual addition inside `torch.autocast(device_type='cuda', enabled=False)` using `.float()` inputs. CUDA autocast already lists `normalize` and `norm` as float32 operations, but explicit control makes a custom expression’s precision clear. Float32 forward arithmetic cannot guarantee safe gradients when those gradients subsequently pass through float16 tensors. [AMP guidance](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/amp.md), [float32 subregion example](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/amp_examples.html).

Implementation inference: choose a meaningful denominator floor relative to observed residual norms, optionally cap the scale ratio, and initialize the residual gate conservatively. A detached scale can prevent gradients through the norm-matching mechanism, but must still be bounded. Preserve padding masks and identical training/predictor arithmetic; inspect finite outputs and gradients at zero and near-zero residuals. These are numerical safeguards within one HSTU network; no backbone or baseline-loss replacement is required.
